articles.title: LIV Golf 2.0 ya tiene luz verde pero está que trina con el Circuito Europeo
articles.standfirst: El tribunal de quiebras permite a LIV Golf su reestructuración, pero desde la superliga denuncia que el DP World Tour ha querido interferir en su proceso
articles.summary: El tribunal de quiebras permite a LIV Golf su reestructuración, pero desde la superliga denuncia que el DP World Tour ha querido interferir en su proceso
articles.body: Sobre el papel, hoy es un gran día para LIV Golf. El juez encargado de su caso de quiebra ha aprobado la reestructuración empresarial junto a BC Partners -el inversor-, superando así un obstáculo significativo, pues ahora podrán gestionar el paquete de financiación propuesto de 300 millones de dólares y crear una nueva estructura. Eso sí, los abogados de LIV han declarado en el tribunal de quiebras que “anticipan que la decisión se tomará para finales de mes” en lo que se refiere a la disolución o continuación con LIV 2.0. Dicho representantes legales también han expresado su malestar con las medidas que va tomar el DP World Tour para de alguna forma torpedearlos. En cualquier caso, si LIV Golf esperaba alfombra roja para su nueva etapa es que parecen haber olvidado su pasado. Un circuito creado a base de talonario, gracias a que arrebató talento a sus competidores, es difícil que vaya a recibir alguna ayuda por parte de estos ahora. Sin la financiación del Fondo de Inversión de Arabia Saudí (PIF), la superliga parte de una posición muy débil. En este sentido, el DP World Tour, aunque no cuente con músculo financiero, tiene un arma muy poderosa que puede sentenciar al LIV. Lo dejó claro su director ejecutivo, Guy Kinnings, el lunes en BBC Sports: "Los jugadores necesitan tomar una decisión. Como hemos dicho durante muchos años, tenemos reglas y regulaciones que están ahí para proteger nuestro Tour y que todos nuestros miembros deben respetar. Los jugadores que no estén dispuestos a cumplir con nuestras reglas y regulaciones no deberían buscar unirse a nuestro Tour". Es decir, el DPWT no dejará que ninguno de sus miembros pueda alternar con torneos del LIV y se terminó el acuerdo por un año al que había llegado con algunos golfistas. Esto nos lleva a la queja hoy de los abogados de LIV que, aunque han conseguido una victoria en los tribunales, parece que no las tienen todas consigo tras la maniobra del DP World Tour. Esto han declarado: “Seguimos monitoreando esta situación muy de cerca, y francamente, nos preocupa bastante […] Francamente, el momento en particular nos parece un claro intento de interferir en nuestro proceso, con nuestros jugadores y potencialmente con nuestra reorganización […] La libertad del jugador es la razón por la que se creó LIV Golf, y es la base de LIV Golf 2.0. […] Es lamentable que otro circuito tome una visión opuesta y presione a nuestros jugadores con una falsa elección”.

articles.title: LIV golf: Organisation concerned by DP Tour's 'attempt to interfere' in player discussions
articles.summary: LIV Golf accuses the DP World Tour of a "clear attempt to interfere" with its restructuring process, after the European tour said it would refuse membership to anyone playing on the breakaway LIV circuit next season.
articles.body:
LIV Golf has accused the DP World Tour of a "clear attempt to interfere" with its restructuring process, after the European tour said it would refuse membership to anyone playing on the breakaway circuit next season.

During a court hearing on Wednesday, the attorney representing LIV said that the organisation was "quite concerned" by the stance taken by the rival DP World Tour.

Rob Fitzgerald of Gibson Dunn, the attorney representing LIV, also said that the organisation would know by the end of the month if it could continue in a 'LIV 2.0' guise.

"We're continuing to monitor this situation very closely and we're quite concerned by it frankly," said Fitzgerald of the DP World Tour's position.

"The timing in particular strikes us as a clear attempt to interfere with our process with our players and potentially our reorganisation writ large.

"It also raises a lot of the same anti-competitive concerns that LIV has expressed previously regarding the way competing leagues have sought to box out and punish market participants, namely these players, from participating in LIV and really only LIV."

DP World Tour declined to comment on Fitzgerald's statement, but Guy Kinnings, its CEO, told BBC Sport on Monday that "players need to make a choice," toughening the organisation's policy on playing across the tours.

In previous years, conditional releases were struck with some top players - including Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton - enabling them to play on both the DP World Tour and LIV.

"Player freedom is the reason LIV Golf was created, and it's the foundation of LIV Golf 2.0, a league built around its players," Fitzgerald added as he continued his argument in court.

"LIV has been vocal in its belief in free agency and that the best players should have greater flexibility to compete across the ecosystem. It's unfortunate that another tour is taking an opposite view and pressuring our players with false choice."

Judge Michael B. Kaplan, overseeing proceedings in the New Jersey Bankruptcy Court, replied: "The comments I have read do raise concerns."

Responding to Kaplan's request for clarity on the timeline of LIV 2.0's creation, Fitzgerald said the "two critical pieces" were structural, relating to the investment from BC Partners , and having "sufficient number of players to have a bona fide golf league signed up by 25th of this month".

"We are working hard around the clock both on the player front and on the structural front," added Fitzgerald.

Asked when he would be able to advise the court "one way or the other" whether LIV was "toggling to a wind-down" or going forward, Fitzgerald said: "We would anticipate that decision will be made by the end of the month.

"Once we have full clarity on LIV 2.0, the debtors will need to very shortly begin making payments to host sites, vendors and other parties, so that we can schedule and prepare for LIV 2.0 events that we anticipate will take place shortly following the emergence."

LIV filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States in September after Saudi Arabia withdrew its multibillion-dollar funding.

As part of the court-supervised "restructuring process", which the organisation hopes to conclude in early 2027, player contracts have been "rejected" and no players are obligated to be part of LIV going forward.

During Wednesday's hearing, 19 player contracts - including those of Bryson DeChambeau and Dustin Johnson - were rejected, after having been adjourned from a hearing last week because those players wanted clarity that contract rejection would enable them to have conversations with third parties about their futures.

LIV recruited a number of high profile players following its launch in 2021, but now owes its participants at least $45m (£33m).

Current Race to Dubai leader Patrick Reed, who left LIV in January, has said he was accepted "from day one" after rejoining the European tour.

"This year fully playing on this tour only has been something I've really enjoyed and I feel like the guys have enjoyed having me come over and playing," said Reed.

"I don't feel any different. I feel like the guys have accepted me from day one.

"I can see how some of the guys would sit there and have an issue with guys coming over and just playing the big events.

"I've come over and played everything from big events, small events, events in the middle. I feel like it hasn't been any different for me."

Meanwhile, six-time major winner Rory McIlroy said that LIV was in "such a state of flux" and that the DP World Tour had been "more than accommodating" to the players seeking to leave the competition.

"The DP World Tour are well within their rights to change the rules and regulations," said McIlroy in his press conference prior to the Thursday start of the DP World India Championship.

"This is a way to protect their business and to make the tour as strong as possible."

On Tuesday he told Bloomberg he would vote to have LIV Golf defectors back on the PGA Tour and believed the breakaway circuit was no longer a threat to traditional tours.

articles.title: Reform faces criticism after councillors filmed making racist comments
articles.summary: Reform says all of those people filmed by ITV are under investigation having resigned or been suspended.
articles.body:
Warning: This report contains racist and offensive language.

Reform UK has said "there is no room for racism" in its party after ITV News broadcast undercover filming, gathered over a year, of some of its councillors and candidates using racist, violent and sexist language.

In the film, Undercover: A Year in Reform, a Reform councillor and deputy mayor of Solihull is recorded calling Asian homeowners "parasites".

Labour described the investigation as "truly sickening" adding: "Nigel Farage can't shrug these latest revelations off as being a few bad apples."

A Reform spokesman said: "Where members, activists and councillors have clearly behaved inappropriately, investigations have commenced" and that in some cases there had been suspensions.

The spokesman added that the party had improved its procedures but some individuals who did not share their values would occasionally make it through vetting.

ITV's filming involved eight figures in Reform – the BBC does not know how many it spoke to in total.

Reform says the people filmed by ITV are all under investigation, and have already either resigned or been suspended.

ITV News says it had reporters undercover with Reform UK candidates and councillors across England and Wales running up to the elections in May and four by-election campaigns this year and last.

These reporters joined a Reform councillor, Alan Feeney, in Solihull, in the West Midlands, where he was campaigning to retain his seat on the council, having defected from the Conservative Party in 2025.

He told undercover reporters the area has been "infested" with Asian families, and called them "absolute parasites".

Later in the film, he is recorded saying: "I'd be saying no more than one per cent of British population can be non-white."

The BBC has tried to contact Feeney for a response. ITV has reported that on Monday evening he had "mutually agreed" to resign from Reform UK, citing "personal reasons," and would be continuing as an independent councillor.

Reform Party leader Nigel Farage has repeatedly said he wants to get rid of those he has called "bad apples."

Two years ago he said he didn't want Reform to be "a sectarian or racially based party in any way at all".

"I'm going to be absolutely ruthless about it," he said.

In a statement released after ITV's film was broadcast, Reform said the party "had improved and prioritised its vetting procedures, but from time to time, a handful of individuals who do not share our values will initially make it through vetting".

The Conservatives said: "Nigel Farage promised to make Reform ready for government. These sorry individuals are proof he has failed."

Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey said: "This is chilling. I feel for anyone watching this tonight who is frightened to see such racism and hatred festering in their community."

A Green Party spokesman said: "Vilifying migrants and Muslims is Reform's main focus, and these racist comments reflect party policy."

Bigots not welcome in Reform UK, says Nigel Farage

articles.title: Vikings legend still thinks about missing out on the rushing record
articles.summary: Former Vikings RB Adrian Peterson still thinks he could have broken the single-season rushing record with another opportunity in 2012.
articles.body:
Former Minnesota Vikings running back Adrian Peterson produced one of the greatest rushing seasons in NFL history in 2012. After returning from a torn ACL suffered on Christmas Eve in 2011, Peterson came back stronger than ever, running for 2,097 yards.

His best moment came in Week 17 against the Green Bay Packers. The Vikings needed to win to make the playoffs, and everyone expected Peterson, who entered the game 208 yards short of Eric Dickerson's single-season rushing record, to be the focal point of the offense again.

Even though the Packers knew Peterson was getting the ball, he still ran for 199 yards and scored two touchdowns (one receiving). Tied at 34 with 26 seconds left in regulation, Peterson took a handoff and burst through the line of scrimmage, evading Green Bay defenders en route to a 26-yard run that set Minnesota up at the Packers' 12-yard line.

Head coach Leslie Frazier let the clock run down to three seconds before calling a timeout. Then kicker Blair Walsh came in to boot the 29-yard field goal through to send the Vikings to the playoffs.

14 years later, Peterson still wishes he had another opportunity before that field goal to break the record.

"Hindsight when I think about, I'm like, 'God, dog, Coach Frazier, man, there [were] like 20 seconds left before I made that last run,'" Peterson told Jordan Schultz in an interview this week. "We could've called a timeout and given me another... run or two to get [the record]."

This was a criticism from fans at the time, though it never really made sense. Had Minnesota elected to call timeout and tried another run with Peterson, there was no guarantee he wouldn't have fumbled it, as that had been an issue throughout his career.

There could also have been any number of penalties, like a false start or holding that would have pushed Walsh back further. Worse yet, there could have been a risk of injury in a moment where the Vikings were in good position for a game-winning field goal.

Peterson came close to the record, and it would have been awesome to see him break it. But even if he wishes the end of the game had played out a little differently, the reality of the situation made it virtually impossible to accommodate the star running back.

articles.title: Will Zalatoris to undergo another major back surgery, will miss 2027 PGA Tour season: 'I've been through four years of hell'
articles.summary: Will Zalatoris is preparing for his third major back surgeries in the past four years.
articles.body:
Will Zalatoris will miss even more time due to his lingering back injury.

Zalatoris revealed on Wednesday at the media day for the PGA Tour's Austin Championship that he will undergo a spinal-fusion surgery late next month. That means that Zalatoris will miss the entire 2027 campaign.

It marks the third major back surgery Zalatoris has undergone since 2023.

"I've been through four years of hell, so it's good to have something that will hopefully correct it," Zalatoris said, via Golf.com . "It's not something you want to do, but when you have three Tour physical therapists tell you it needs to be done at some time, you go ahead and do it."

Zalatoris missed several months during the 2022 campaign due to two herniated discs in his back. Then, just before the Masters the following spring , he withdrew and underwent surgery on his back. That ended the 2023 campaign.

The injury has essentially lingered ever since. He said that he hurt his back again playing in San Antonio at the Valero Texas Open.

He recovered after his most recent back surgery last year and appeared in four events this season, but missed the cut in two of them and then finished T67 at the Valero Texas Open in April. He's not played competitively since.

Zalatoris was once a very promising golfer on Tour. He picked up his inaugural win at the 2022 FedEx St. Jude Championship, and he finished second at the Masters in 2021. Zalatoris had a stretch in which he finished top 10 in six of seven major championships, including a playoff loss at the PGA Championship in 2022 and a T2 run at the U.S. Open a month later.

But Zalatoris has missed the cut in his last four major championship outings, and has only played in 15 tournaments over the past two seasons. He's plummeted to No. 610 in the Official World Golf Rankings, too.

While Zalatoris will play in Austin, that'll be it until 2028. Hopefully by then, he said, he'll be in a much better spot.

"It's all connected together, and I just want to get it fixed," he said. "I can't promise anybody anything because of what I've been through. I'm the oldest 30-year-old you will ever meet."

articles.title: Rory McIlroy Chases Race To Dubai Title Against Patrick Reed
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy hunts a record-equaling Race to Dubai title in New Delhi, facing his longtime rival Patrick Reed in a showdown with no middle ground.
articles.body:
Rory McIlroy has a specific goal in mind this week in New Delhi. He wants to capture his eighth Race to Dubai title. That would tie the all-time record held by Colin Montgomerie. But the path to that trophy is blocked by a familiar face. Patrick Reed currently leads the standings, while McIlroy has won the race for four consecutive years.

The two men are meeting on a new battleground in India, a place Reed had visited before this event existed. They share a decade of history, from the 2016 Ryder Cup to the 2018 Masters. Now they are back chasing the same points.

The dynamic between these two has shifted dramatically since the golf world fractured. After Reed departed the LIV Golf league and received a PGA Tour suspension, an opportunity arose for him to compete on the DP World Tour. He has won on the circuit since his return. McIlroy, meanwhile, supported the creation of the DP World India Championship to hunt new experiences.

Yahoo Sports reports that on Tuesday at the Delhi Golf Club, the pair exchanged a smile and a short conversation during a photo opportunity. They have been complimentary all season. Reed noted at the BMW PGA Championship that he relishes the chance to compete against McIlroy. "Any time I get to go play against Rory, it's always fun because that means you get to play some amazing golf," Reed said.

McIlroy stated that he requires no additional motivation to commit fully. "Yeah, look, I'm motivated regardless of who it is," he said at Wentworth.

While the players compete for points, the broader war over the sport's future appears to be ending. McIlroy is confident the threat from the rebel league is gone for good. In New Delhi, while speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum, he addressed the probability of a second LIV Golf iteration launching.

McIlroy stated at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi that launching version 2.0 of LIV seems difficult, noting that with each passing day, another former LIV player declares they will not return to LIV 2.0. He believes the league mismanaged its massive financial resources. "LIV had probably like half of a good idea that was executed pretty poorly," McIlroy said. He argued the capital could have been used to partner with governing bodies instead of enriching pros who were already wealthy.

The landscape has changed with players like Jon Rahm, David Puig, and Adrian Meronk reportedly leaving the Saudi-backed league. Even Sergio Garcia had his contract terminated. McIlroy recalled his early stance against the breakaway. "Tiger and I, at the very start back in 2022 when this thing kicked off, we were certainly the two that were maybe the most vocal against it," McIlroy said.

Now, the choice for any player considering a return to the breakaway is stark. "You see Guy Kinnings coming out this week and saying that if LIV does go ahead in this 2.0 version, players that are thinking of going that direction, they're gonna have to make a choice," McIlroy said. "It's either you play LIV 2.0, and you can't play the DP World Tour, or you play the DP World Tour, and you can't play LIV 2.0. But I think this period of trying to double dip and do both is over."

This week's event in India represents more than just a tournament. It is the culmination of a decade-long rivalry and a test of the unified game. Reed is looking to become only the second American to win the Race to Dubai, joining Collin Morikawa. McIlroy is just one title shy of the record he covets. The fact that they are both there, competing on the same course, signals a new era.

The tension that once existed between the two tours is gone. The focus is now on performance and the points that matter most. Reed holds the lead, but McIlroy has the momentum and the experience of winning this race multiple times. The handshake in New Delhi was a sign of respect, but the competition on the course will be fierce. Both men are chasing a legacy-defining trophy.

The DP World Tour schedule continues with high stakes for both golfers. The Race to Dubai concludes at the end of the season, making every shot in India critical. McIlroy's comments suggest he sees the future of golf as stable and unified. The departure of major players from LIV and the bankruptcy filing in September have accelerated that shift.

If the league tries to reboot, it will face a wall of players who want to return to the traditional order. For now, the attention remains on the green in New Delhi. The battle for the title is on, and the history between these two rivals will play out in real time.
